title: Quantitative aspects of electrolysis
competency: Use Faraday's first and second laws to calculate masses, volumes, charges and currents in electrolysis.

keywords.def: The charge on one mole of electrons: F = 96 500 C/mol.
The mass deposited is proportional to the charge passed: m = MIt/(nF).
The same charge deposits masses in the ratio of their equivalent masses: m₁/E₁ = m₂/E₂.

en.text: The mass of substance formed at an electrode is proportional to the charge passed, Q = It. One mole of electrons carries 96 500 C (the Faraday constant). So moles of electrons = It/F, moles of product = moles of electrons ÷ n from the half-reaction, and m = MIt/(nF), with t in seconds.

am.text: በኤሌክትሮድ የሚፈጠረው ብዛት ከተላለፈው ቻርጅ Q = It ጋር ተመጣጣኝ ነው፤ m = MIt/(nF)።

screens.title: Copper plating
screens.ask: Change the current and the time. How much copper is deposited (Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu)?
screens.note: m = MIt/(nF), with t in seconds.

screens.title: Faraday's first law
paras: m ∝ Q, and Q = It (coulombs = amperes × seconds).
Moles of product = moles of e⁻ ÷ electrons per formula (from the half-reaction).

screens.title: Key words
defs: The charge on one mole of electrons: F = 96 500 C/mol.
The mass deposited is proportional to the charge passed: m = MIt/(nF).

screens.text: How many moles of electrons are needed to deposit 1 mole of aluminium?
screens.clue: Look at the charge on the ion.

screens.ask: Na₂SO₄ solution is electrolyzed for 2 h at 10 A. Volume of H₂ at 25 °C and 1 atm (24.5 L/mol) ≈ ___ L (1 decimal place)

en.text: When the same charge passes through cells in series, the masses deposited are proportional to the equivalent masses (molar mass ÷ electrons per ion): m₁/E₁ = m₂/E₂. Equivalently, the same number of moles of electrons reaches every cathode.

am.text: አንድ አይነት ቻርጅ በተከታታይ ሴሎች ሲያልፍ የሚፈጠሩት ብዛቶች ከኢኩቫለንት ብዛታቸው ጋር ይመጣጠናሉ፡ m₁/E₁ = m₂/E₂።

screens.title: Silver or copper?
screens.ask: AgNO₃ and CuSO₄ cells are joined in series, so the same charge passes through both. Which metal is deposited in greater mass?
screens.after: Each electron deposits one Ag (108 g/mol) but only half a Cu (63.5 ÷ 2 = 31.75 g).

screens.title: Faraday's second law
paras: Same charge through cells in series.
Masses are in the ratio of equivalent masses: m₁/E₁ = m₂/E₂.
Equivalent mass E = molar mass ÷ electrons per ion.

screens.title: Key word
defs: The same charge deposits masses in the ratio of their equivalent masses: m₁/E₁ = m₂/E₂.

screens.ask: The equivalent mass of copper in Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu (63.5 g/mol) is ___ g
screens.clue: Divide by the electrons per ion.

notes.text: p.81: F = 96 500 C per mole of electrons (C/mol; more precisely 96 485). "Valence n" means electrons per ion; t must be in seconds.
Example 2.3: Mg and Al cannot be deposited from aqueous solutions; read the states as molten. Example 2.4: the overall equation has "→" where "+" belongs and should use (l).
Figure 2.6 label "Cu₂SO₄" should be CuSO₄; p.83 prints "2.44 × 103" for 2.44 × 10³.
